name: diya-submit
description: Work out a UK VAT return from your saved books, check the nine boxes, then open the link the assistant gives you and file it yourself on the Submit page. Read your stored VAT receipts afterwards.

interface.shortDescription: UK VAT return from your books
interface.longDescription: Work out a UK VAT return from a book saved in DIY Accounting Submit. List your books, open one, and derive the nine VAT boxes for a quarter with the journal lines behind them. Ask for the link to the VAT form with the figures filled in, then open it and file the return yourself in the browser, where you tick the declaration. Afterwards, read your stored VAT receipts. No tool in this plugin files a return or pays HMRC. A person signs in to an existing DIY Accounting Submit account that holds a saved book.
capabilities: List the books saved in your account
Open a book and read its checks
Derive the nine VAT boxes for a quarter
Give a link to file the return in the browser
defaultPrompt: Derive the VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025

publication.release_notes: First release. List the books saved in your DIY Accounting Submit account, open one, and work out the nine VAT boxes for a quarter with the lines behind them. Get a link to the VAT form with the figures filled in, then check and file the return yourself on the Submit site. Read your stored VAT receipts afterwards.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. A person signs in to an existing DIY Accounting Submit account and uses what that account already has.

positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists the saved books by name, BrickWork Pro Ltd and Precision Code Ltd.

positive.description: Open the BrickWork Pro Ltd book
positive.prompt: Open the BrickWork Pro Ltd book.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant opens BrickWork Pro Ltd and says the business, the period covered, the line count and the book checks.

positive.prompt: Derive the VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant shows the nine VAT boxes with their amounts and points out lines in the quarter worth checking before filing.

positive.prompt: Give me the link to file it.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant gives a link to the VAT form on the Submit site with the figures filled in, and says the person checks and files in the browser.
The assistant says the account has no stored VAT receipts.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin files a return. The assistant does not file it: it offers the link from prepare_vat_return, says the person ticks the declaration and files in the browser, and says nothing has been filed.
negative.prompt: File my VAT return for me.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin pays HMRC or anyone else. The assistant says it cannot pay. It says the person pays HMRC through their own bank or HMRC's service.
The plugin offers VAT tools only. The assistant says it cannot file company accounts with this plugin, and it does not say that it filed them.
